subject: Demo request: GitHub integration + OSS workflow
messages:
From: Natalie Brooks <natalie@codecommons.org>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Demo request: GitHub integration + OSS workflow

Hi Karthik,

I signed up for a trial on the Redwood site this morning and poked around the dashboard — nice work! We're an engineering team at CodeCommons (open-source infra for civic projects) and we're evaluating options for running inference on PR checks and as part of a GitHub Actions workflow. A few quick things I want to confirm before we block a demo:

- Can Redwood be used with self-hosted runners and still keep repo/code artifacts private (we're sensitive to leaking code to a hosted model)?
- What GitHub permissions/tokens do you need for the integration? We try to follow the least-privilege principle.
- Do you have examples of automating comment-based checks and reruns (e.g., rerun on a new commit)?

I can do a quick demo next week — my timezone is PDT. If possible I'd like a technical person on the call (we'll likely bring two engineers).

Repo link: https://github.com/codecommons/example-repo

Thanks,
Natalie Brooks
Director of Engineering, CodeCommons
-----
Attachment: none (will attach sample repo if helpful)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Brooks <natalie@codecommons.org>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request: GitHub integration + OSS workflow

Hi Natalie — great to meet you and thanks for signing up. Glad you found the dashboard useful.

Short answers up front: yes, you can keep inference in a private environment (Private/VPC) and integrate with self-hosted runners; token scopes are customizable and we have patterns for least-privilege installs. I can walk through the tech flow in the demo.

Would any of these times work for a 30-minute session (all PDT)?
- Tue 2026-10-13 10:00 — 10:30
- Wed 2026-10-14 09:00 — 09:30
- Wed 2026-10-14 11:00 — 11:30

If you prefer, grab a slot: https://calendly.com/redwood-sdr/30min

If it helps, I can include Marissa Cole (AE) to cover billing/entitlements and a short rollout plan. Also attaching a one-pager that summarizes our GitHub integration options.

Agenda suggestion (we can edit):
1) Quick intros & what you're trying to accomplish (5m)
2) Integration flow: runners, webhooks, and token scopes (10m)
3) Demo of a PR check + comment-triggered rerun (10m)
4) Next steps: security, pricing, and trial extension (5m)

Attachment: redwood-github-integration-one-pager.pdf

Best,
Karthik Iyer
SDR, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0196

Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the quick reply. Wed 2026-10-14 11:00 PDT works for us (we'll have two engineers: me and Raj Patel). Please include Marissa if she has bandwidth.

A couple of specific items we'd like covered so we can make the most of 30 minutes:
- How webhook delivery is retried/observed (we often run into flaky webhook delivery from internal runners)
- Whether Redwood ever stores repository blobs or if everything stays on customer infra (compliance question)
- Example least-privilege token scopes for read-only checks vs. write/commenting

I've uploaded a trimmed sample of our test repo to an archive (attached) — it's not private-sensitive but mirrors our CI layout. Also: can you confirm if you support GitHub App installation vs. PAT? We prefer the App model if available.

Attached: example-codecommons-repo.zip

Thanks — see you Wed 11:00 PDT.

—Natalie
